title: Choose the visual world for Phone Health (re-roll 1)
question: Fresh hand. The roll assigned the Rack Bezel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Rack Bezel
options.lineage: 1U/2U rack-server front panels: status LCD, component LED grid, drive-bay caddies, colour-coded touch points
options.thesis: Treat the phone as the server it is: the app is its front bezel, and the bezel's two-line status LCD states the verdict the way a real server does, backlight blue when healthy, amber on a fault.
options.viewport: Top: a two-line character LCD across the full width, blue-lit 'SYSTEM OK · SERVING 2/2', switching to amber 'CHECK BATTERY 46C' on a fault. Under it, the component grid: one labelled bay per subsystem (BATTERY, THERMAL, STORAGE, MEMORY, NETWORK, SERVICES, LOGGER), each with its LED and live reading. Below the grid, the 7-day activity panel: one LED row per day. Service tag at the foot. Bottom bar: Status / Readings / History / Tests as bay tabs.
options.risk: Grey hardware chrome can tip into skeuomorphic costume. It has to stay flat and functional: the LED, the reading and the label do the work, and the bezel only frames them.

raised.raise: Fixed digit positions: every reading uses tabular digits at a fixed width and precision, so a value changing from 9.8 to 10.2 never shifts its row.
State without colour: a bay in warning also carries a diagonal hatch across its LED window, so amber vs green survives colour-blindness and sunlight.
Trace the load: every amber bay opens to its cause and its remedy, never a bare warning.
Numbered procedure: the hardware tests run as a service procedure, steps 01 to 09 in a strict margin column.
One state drives everything: a single OK/CHECK/FAULT state sets the LCD backlight, the LEDs and the label ink together, never independently.

options.label: Status Page Ledger
options.lineage: public status pages self-hosters read every day (90-day uptime bars, incident log)
options.thesis: Publish the phone's own status page to itself: one uptime bar per component, and an incident log written in plain sentences.
options.viewport: 'All systems operational' banner, then one row per component with a 7-day tick bar, then 'Past incidents' in dated sentences.
options.risk: The most familiar card here: it's what Uptime Kuma and every status page already look like.

options.label: Camcorder Viewfinder
options.thesis: The app is a viewfinder on the phone: readouts pinned to the four corners, zebra stripes crawl over any reading that's over its limit.
options.viewport: Verdict centred inside focus brackets; battery, thermal, services and uptime readouts one per corner; zebra over anything hot or down.
options.case: Zebra-on-over-limit is a crisp signal that doesn't rely on colour (holds clarity); nobody hosting a server sees themselves behind a camcorder (loses audience).
options.risk: A recording-camera metaphor on a device that isn't filming anything.

options.label: Nixie Lab Counter
options.case: A reword of last round's cathode card; one orange can't carry severity.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.case: Beautiful, but photographers' notation, not servers'.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.case: A force diagram with no forces to show.
options.kept: Trace every load to its counterforce.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.case: A sequence you learn, not a state you glance at.
options.kept: Numbered steps in a strict margin column.

options.label: Generative Identity
options.case: Novelty identity for a tool that should look the same every morning.
options.kept: One state drives every surface in lockstep.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Material 3 device-care dashboard (Samsung Device care, Google's battery health screens), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A big circular health score, a row of tonal cards per subsystem, bottom navigation bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the phone's own Device care screen by design.
